# Comparing slices

Element-by-element equality, the first difference and lexicographic order between two slices.

<h2 id="mismatch"><code>Mismatch&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Mismatch<T>(left: T[..], right: T[..]) -> uint?
```

The index of the first position where `left` and `right` differ.
Both are borrowed and read. Reports `none` when neither runs out before a difference is found and the two are
equal for their whole common length — so two slices of different lengths that agree on the shorter one report
the shorter length, and two identical slices report `none`.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the shorter length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L194)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description              |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------ |
| `left`  | `T[..]` | one of the two sequences |
| `right` | `T[..]` | the other                |

**Returns**: the first index where the two differ, or `none` when neither runs out first

<h2 id="sequence-equal"><code>SequenceEqual&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SequenceEqual<T>(left: T[..], right: T[..]) -> bool
```

Whether `left` and `right` hold the same elements in the same order.
Both are borrowed and read. Different lengths are never equal, and two empty slices are, whatever their data
pointers hold.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the shorter length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L214)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description              |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------ |
| `left`  | `T[..]` | one of the two sequences |
| `right` | `T[..]` | the other                |

**Returns**: whether both hold the same elements in the same order

<h2 id="compare"><code>Compare&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Compare<T>(left: T[..], right: T[..]) -> Ordering
```

How `left` orders against `right`, element by element.
Both are borrowed and read. The comparison is lexicographic, which is the order a dictionary uses: the first
position where the two differ decides, and if neither differs before one runs out, the shorter is the smaller.
Two equal-length slices that never differ are `Equal`.
Requires `<` and `==` on the element type. Use [`CompareBy`](/docs/api/algorithms/comparing#compare-by) where the element has no ordering of its own or the
wanted order is not its own.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the shorter length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L231)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description              |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------ |
| `left`  | `T[..]` | one of the two sequences |
| `right` | `T[..]` | the other                |

**Returns**: how `left` orders against `right`, comparing element by element then by length

<h2 id="compare-by"><code>CompareBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CompareBy<T>(
    left: T[..],
    right: T[..],
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> Ordering
```

How `left` orders against `right`, with `compare` deciding each pair.
Both slices are borrowed and read; `compare` is called at most once per position of the shorter one. Lexicographic
exactly as [`Compare`](/docs/api/algorithms/comparing#compare) is, and the way to order a sequence whose elements have no `<` of their own — or to order it
by something other than their own.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the shorter length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L255)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `left`    | `T[..]`                  | one of the two sequences                  |
| `right`   | `T[..]`                  | the other                                 |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: how `left` orders against `right` under `compare`, then by length
